messages:
maria: Heads up — Stonebridge legal pinged us asking to pin traffic to their dedicated cluster via a header (they want an escape hatch for migration).

jin: Do they want this permanent or temporary?

maria: Temporary for the initial migration window (they said 3 days) but legal also asked to retain the option for future ad-hoc pins.

maria: Example header they sent:

maria: ```\nX-Redwood-Route: org=stonebridge;mode=private;ttl=259200\n```

sam: Console UX concern — we can't just accept arbitrary headers. Need an approval flow + clear visibility of cost and telemetry.

tess: Security: if we accept an override header it must be signed (HMAC with customer key or a signed JWT). Otherwise this is a spoof/drift risk.

jin: From runtime side: precedence rules should be explicit. Proposal: header-driven pin only applies if (1) header HMAC verifies using org KMS key, (2) org is in an allowlist for ad-hoc pins, and (3) the console shows an active approval record. Otherwise ignore header.

maria: Also important: billing/quota implications. If they route to Dedicated it consumes capacity and could affect other tenants.

jin: We'll emit trace tags: route_reason=org_manual_pin and route_target=dedicated:<pool>. Charge will be billed to the org's billing account. If request would exceed committed capacity, return 429 / 403 with clear error.

sam: UX proposal: "Approve override" modal in Console with fields: TTL (default 72h), approvers, reason, estimated hourly cost delta, and required security proof (signed header schema). Button creates an approval record and returns a signed token the gateway can verify.

maria: Ops opened a ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/RED-4321 — linking the customer request.

ops-bot: [auto] Created approval record RED-4321, status=PENDING, approvers=[jin,tess], created_by=maria

tess: I can approve if we have documented HMAC scheme and KMS key. Also require audit log retention 13 months for legal.

jin: Follow-ups for engineering:
- runtime: verify HMAC/JWT and strip header after routing to avoid downstream leakage
- gateway: emit structured telemetry fields (route.source=org_pin, route.approver=NAME, route.ttl)
- console: create approval record and store signed token to hand back to client
- ops: auto-revoke on TTL expiry and emit revocation event

sam: I'll mock the Console modal and put in the cost estimation widget. Also add a warning: "This will route traffic to a dedicated pool and may affect capacity/SLAs." :warning:

maria: Can we restrict this to enterprise tier only? Stonebridge is enterprise but we should gate by plan.

jin: Yes — feature-flagged and allowlist + per-org capability check.

sam: UX detail: show the active approval badge next to the org in the org management page, and a quick link to revoke.

maria: Sounds good. Maria -> will update customer and request they submit a signed header and provide approver names.

jin: I'll spike the runtime check today and push a small gateway guard. If it looks fine we can wire console next week.

tess: I'll draft the security doc for HMAC/JWT header verification and retention requirements.

maria: Great. Ping me when you have the mock and the small gateway PR. :thumbsup:
